source.title: Improving Implicit Regularization of SGD with Preconditioning for Least Square Problems
source.authors: Junwei Su; Chuan Wu; Le Zheng; Di-Fan Zou

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends work on SGD's implicit regularization to preconditioned SGD in Gaussian least-squares problems and reports theoretical and empirical generalization results. The tested setting is outside the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports empirical comparisons in Figure 1 and describes their outcomes in Section 4.5. The theoretical bounds and results cited from earlier work are not separate empirical result rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares preconditioned SGD with SGD and ridge regression in least-squares problems. Its results do not test any V1–V8: preconditioning in linear regression does not establish V4's adaptive-optimizer comparison on image or language benchmarks, and the ReLU-regression appendix contains no width sweep relevant to V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. More precisely, the authors establish comparability up to constant factors under stated assumptions, sufficiently large sample sizes, and suitable hyperparameter choices; comparisons with preconditioned ridge concern a specified family. They also establish guarantees for covariance estimation from unlabeled data and report supporting synthetic experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies single-pass, constant-step-size, tail-averaged preconditioned SGD on Gaussian least-squares problems and compares excessive risk with ridge regression; this differs from the claim versions' deep-network settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.5 reports that PreSGD and PreSGD-Est match ridge when ridge outperforms SGD and further improve performance when SGD matches or beats ridge across six Gaussian least-squares instances.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitably tuned covariance-based preconditioning can improve test MSE over standard SGD in these Gaussian least-squares instances, including when estimated using additional unlabeled data.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 4.3–4.6 establish excess-risk comparisons with standard ridge and a specified family of preconditioned ridge estimators.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated least-squares assumptions and sufficiently large sample sizes, suitable preconditioning and step-size choices allow single-pass tail-averaged SGD to match ridge excess risk up to constant factors, including with estimated covariance.

record.peer_reviewed: SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science
record.problems: The empirical study uses Gaussian least-squares problems with dimension 200 and reports averages over 10 runs. Figure 1 values are not stated in the text, and the text does not report error bars. Hyperparameters are fine-tuned for best performance.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy in the same architectures and training recipes.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on image and language benchmarks under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, small-data regimes, underfitting, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T3 is inappropriate because no claim version is tested in the new setting. The cannot_determine states concern V1–V8, not whether the authors report improvements in their separate optimization comparison. Missing PreSGD-Est rows do not constitute missing evidence for any version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in the listed image models.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning and benchmark conditions.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout and weight-decay effects in classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: Preconditioned-SGD (PreSGD)
rows.stage_stated: single-pass SGD with constant step size and tail-averaging
rows.operation_detail: Train with proposed preconditioning G = (βH + I)−1; β and step size are fine-tuned.
rows.measure: Excessive risk measured as MSE on an independent test set of size 1000
rows.uncertainty: Plots averaged over 10 independent runs; error bars not stated.
rows.note: Authors state that Ridge outperforms SGD in this case and PreSGD achieves comparable performance to Ridge; no plotted values are transcribed.
rows.check: Own-method performance comparison outside all versions; exclude from claim-evidence rows. PreSGD is an algorithm, not a model. The plotted measure is test MSE, not excess risk as defined in Section 3; numerical curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.
